newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN COMMITTEE SEEKS 1 MLN BALES EXPORT RELEASE.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN COMMITTEE SEEKS 1 MLN BALES EXPORT RELEASE.

text.p: India must release at least one million 170-kg bales of cotton for export ahead of the 1997/98 (October/September) season to take care of its surplus, a parliamentary committee said on Tuesday.
The committee of law makers, which studied the problems of cotton growers, suggested in its report that half the quota be given to the state-run Cotton Corporation of India and the rest to others.
According to traders, prospects for the new crop, which will come on to the market in the 1997/98 season, have been bright.
The 1996/97 cotton crop has been estimated at 16.78 million bales, up from the previous year's 16.27 million.
Traders said cotton arrivals indicated that the current year's crop could even touch 17 million bales.
India released 500,000 bales for export before the start of the current season and the move pushed prices up in a market saddled with huge carryover stocks from the previous year.
Traders said India's cotton exports in 1996/97 were expected to be higher at 1.4 million bales compared to 790,000 in the previous season.
India has authorised an export quota of 1.34 million bales for the current season. Of this, 1.15 million bales have been registered and actual shipments till July-end amounted to 900,000 bales.
Traders said they would expect at least 100,000 bales from the remaining 250,000 bales to be shipped before the end of the current season.
Total shipments, including the spillover, would be about 1.4 million bales, they said.
